main.t: One of a pair of irregular bones that form the back quarter of the hard palate (palatine bone).

simpler.t: The palatine bones form the back of the bony roof of your mouth.

deeper.t: They also form small parts of the side walls of the nasal cavity and of the orbit.

facts.t: Its horizontal plate meets its partner in the midline, at the back of the hard palate.
In front of it are the palatine processes of the maxillae.
It is best seen looking at the skull from below.

simpler.t: It sits at the back of the bony roof of your mouth.

deeper.t: The palatine bone also adds a small part to the floor of the orbit, beside the maxilla.

items.name: Horizontal plate
items.t: Its largest region; with its partner it forms the back quarter of the hard palate.

items.name: Nasal part
items.t: Adds small areas to the side walls of the nasal cavity.

items.name: Orbital part
items.t: A small contribution to the orbit.

items.name: Shape
items.t: An irregular bone, paired with its partner.

simpler.t: Its main part is a flat plate at the back of the roof of the mouth.

deeper.t: So it reaches from the roof of the mouth up into the nose and the orbit.

facts.t: With the maxillae, it completes the hard palate, which separates the mouth from the nasal cavity.
A complete palate keeps the mouth and nose apart, so an infant can suckle.

simpler.t: It finishes the roof of your mouth, sealing it off from your nose.

items.name: Maxillae
items.t: Their palatine processes form the front three-quarters of the hard palate.

items.name: Other palatine bone
items.t: Its partner, meeting it in the midline.

items.name: Nasal cavity
items.t: The hard palate forms its floor; the palatine bone adds to its side walls.

items.name: Orbit
items.t: A small part of the floor, beside the maxilla.

simpler.t: It joins the maxillae and its partner to make the roof of the mouth.

facts.t: During development, its horizontal plate and the maxillae’s palatine processes fuse in the midline, forming the hard palate.
Like the other flat bones of the face, it forms directly from membrane (intramembranous ossification).
facts.check: OpenStax 6.4 says the flat bones of the face form from membrane, but 7.5 says the facial bones form from cartilage; which applies to the palatine bone needs an approved source.

items.injury: The two halves of the hard palate fail to fuse during development (cleft palate).
items.damaged: The palatine plates and palatine processes leave a gap in the midline.
items.cannotDo: Suckle well: the infant is at risk of malnutrition until surgery.
items.why: The gap connects the mouth and nasal cavity, so no seal forms.

items.injury: In a severe cleft palate, the gap continues forwards.
items.damaged: The alveolar processes of the maxillae, above the front teeth, also fail to join.
items.cannotDo: Close the upper lip: a cleft lip is also present.
items.why: The lip forms over the joining maxillae at the same time as the palate.

items.q: Explain how the hard palate forms.
model: The right and left maxillae come together in the midline.
The horizontal plates of the palatine bones join behind them.
All four fuse in the midline to form the hard palate.

items.q: Compare cleft lip and cleft palate.
model: Cleft lip: the two sides of the upper lip fail to fuse.
It affects about 1 in 1000 births, mostly males.
Cleft palate: the two halves of the hard palate fail to fuse; about 1 in 2500 births, more often females.
Cleft palate is more severe, as it makes suckling difficult.

items.q: Predict why a baby with a cleft palate struggles to feed.
model: The gap connects the mouth with the nasal cavity.
So the baby cannot seal the mouth.
Without a seal, it cannot suckle well.
Surgical repair is needed to prevent malnutrition.

check.stem: Which part of the hard palate do the palatine bones form?
check.why: Their horizontal plates form the posterior quarter of the hard palate.

check.stem: Which bones join the palatine bones to form the hard palate?
check.why: The palatine processes of the maxillae form the rest of the hard palate.

check.stem: Why does a cleft palate make feeding difficult?
options: The mouth and nose are connected, so no seal forms
check.why: The gap connects the oral and nasal cavities, so suckling is very difficult.
